newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain studies ways to liberalise tabacco sector.
newsitem.headline: Spain studies ways to liberalise tabacco sector.

text.p: Spain's Economy Ministry is working on ways to liberalise the tobacco sector, a ministry source said on Wednesday.

Financial daily Cinco Dias reported on Wednesday that the ministry was set to conclude a draft law to entirely liberalise the sector that would come into effect before the planned privatisation of Tabacalera in 1998. The state still owns 52 percent of the tobacco firm.

"It is true that the government intends to liberalise the sector. The Treasury secretary announced this in January, although it will not be enforced immediately," a ministry source told Reuters in response to reports in the local press.
The report said the government would liberalise imports of raw tobacco from non-EU countries and would end the production monopoly that Tabacalera enjoys.
The source confirmed that the government would maintain the network of state tobacco shops as the main distribution channel for tobacco in Spain.
Analysts believe the latter point is the most important for tobacco business in Spain.

Currently, only Tabacalera supplies the network of 16,000 state outlets, but analysts say liberalisation is necessary to enable the creation of a second distribution network. Other distributors such as gas stations currently have to buy tobacco products from the state network.

"The liberalisation of production in the face of excess capacity in Europe and tobacco imports from non-EU countries do not play an important role in the deregulation of the sector, whose key area remains distribution," said one analyst.
"Before the privatisation (of Tabacalera), the government must open a second distribution network which will certainly impact Tabacalera's business," he added.

Spain's Competition Commission recently forced Tabacalera to supply its own brand products to other distributors, a decision that was appealed by Tabacalera which fears the competition it may face in a business with a turnover of some 700 billion pesetas last year.
By 1115 GMT, Tabacalera shares were 150 pesetas, or 2.03 percent, down at 7,250, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was 0.45 percent up at 6,433.83.
